correctness.rationale: The semisimple decomposition V=ker(1−T)⊕im(1−T) gives component fibers U×W, with connected operation on W. For any set-theoretic quandle homomorphism, fiber transitivity makes the U output a map φ:U→U. Substituting 0 and using invertibility of T and 1−T on W makes each fiber W map additive, hence F_p-linear commuting with T. Cross-fiber preservation forces one common linear part A and translation b: F(u,w)=(φ(u),Aw+b). Idempotency is exactly φ²=φ, A²=A, Ab=0. On the pairwise distinct irreducible F_{p^{e_i}} blocks the commuting endomorphisms have product matrix algebras, and idempotents correspond to invariant images S_i, invariant complements N_i and b_i∈N_i, giving Gaussian(d_i,r_i;q_i)q_i^{(r_i+1)(d_i-r_i)} affine maps. A fixed affine coset gives one b for each complement, yielding the claimed image-refined multiplicities and exhaustive cardinality polynomial. Boundary W=0, Q=1, constants and rank-(Q−1)|W| (Q≥2; q_i≥4 in borderline Q=2) were checked.

value.rationale: For nonconnected finite Alexander quandles, the component labels can evolve by genuinely arbitrary nonlinear set maps, so a linear-only calculation misses most homomorphisms. The semisimple theorem gives a uniform structural decomposition of the whole monoid and exact image-class multiplicities, across all finite prime-field dimensions and nonsplit simple extension blocks. The intrinsic classification can inform quandle algebraic actions, retracts, and image ranks; it is a motivated complete census rather than an arbitrary small example.
